issues.details: The reference contains ten relocation records with numeric type 123. Their Metrowerks/Sony semantics must be proven before linked-byte acceptance. See relocation indices 32125 and 37417-37425 in .agent/REFERENCE_CENSUS.json.
issues.summary: Relocation type 123 semantics remain unresolved

issues.details: debug import-plan for socom:work:debug-type-foundation reports 40 blocking conflicts. 22 of them (CAppCamera, CAssetLib, CCamera, CE3Config, CExitMenu, CGridAtom, CHUD, CLoadMenu, CMD_TABLE, CMenuStateMenu, CMPExitMenu, CNodeAction, CNodeEx, CPickup, CSealUnit, CSnd, CSndInstance, CSubMenu, CValve, DiIntersect, Source, TASK_SELECT) differ only because some compile units emit a class_type with byte_size 0 and no members (an incomplete declaration) beside exactly one complete layout. _conflicts() in tools/_socom/import_plan.py compares (kind, byte_size, members) and so treats the declaration as a second layout. Declarations should be planned as forward declarations of the unique complete definition, not as conflicts.

resolution.summary: tools/_socom/type_identity.py treats size-0, member-less class records as forward declarations; die_identity maps them to the unique complete structural class of that name (or an explicit symbol, spelling, or opaque identity). The foundation plan's 22 declaration-only conflicts are gone.

issues.summary: DWARF planner reports size-0 class declarations as incompatible with their definitions

issues.details: 18 of the 40 foundation-plan conflicts are distinct complete types sharing a DWARF 1 spelling: template instantiations (vector, __vector_imp, compressed_pair, compressed_pair_imp, deque, cdeque, generic_iterator, iterator, node, node_base, pair, basic_filebuf, ctype) and nested or provider types that Metrowerks DWARF 1 emits at compile-unit level without their container (AI_PARAMS has three unrelated layouts in camera.cpp alone; LOD is a 12-byte class and a 1-byte enum; entry, SequenceEntry, _reent 748 vs 752). Identity is the bare name, and compatibility ignores member types, so same-layout instantiations such as vector<int> and vector<CFoo*> are silently unified even where no conflict is reported. Mangled .symtab names recover the qualification, e.g. SetDefaults__Q28CZWeapon9AI_PARAMSF10EQUIP_ITEM (CZWeapon::AI_PARAMS), Q310Metrowerks14range_map<w,w>5entry, Q28Particle16SequenceEntry<f>, Q23std46vector<8AnimType,...>. The planner needs structural identity (member types resolved recursively) plus Metrowerks-demangled qualification from member-function symbols before the foundation plan can be conflict-free.

resolution.summary: Import plan schema 3 groups type DIEs into structural classes (member types, array elements, and enum elements included; pointees by name) and names each class from DWARF method this/parameter links, R5900 call-site this tracking, unique demangled .symtab candidates, or unique spelling. Unproven or contradictory classes get deterministic provisional names under /project/unresolved/ (owner-approved 2026-10-06). The foundation plan has 0 blocking conflicts: 140 method, 146 call-site, 173 symbol, 178 spelling, 108 provisional.

issues.summary: DWARF planner identity collapses template instantiations and flattened nested types

issues.details: _debug_import_plan clears functions and variables for selection=types, but build_import_plan has already filled receipt_scope.functions (879 addresses for socom:work:debug-type-foundation). The apply item's receipt scope would then claim functions the plan never changes; receipt scopes must be limited to the leased scope.

resolution.summary: build_import_plan now omits functions, variables, and receipt_scope.functions for selection=types; receipt_scope.types lists Ghidra paths.

issues.summary: Types-only import plans keep function addresses in their receipt scope

issues.details: Independent review of socom:work:debug-type-foundation (handoff at tracker revision 9) found wrong template names. F1: class socom:type-class:2664c3e891c7b52d9f0a (raw queue) took the sole .symtab candidate std::queue<member-function pointer,...>; JoinRoom__13CZOnlineLobbyFPCc proves it is queue<CZOnlineLobby::LOBBY_STATE> (addiu a0,s3,0x64 then deque<LOBBY_STATE>::push_back). Inlined instantiations never reach .symtab, so a sole symbol candidate does not prove a template name. F2: socom:type-class:d4bacb1e4c865019715b (raw stack) was named stack<unsigned int> while CRdrEditor::addint shows deque<CRDRNodeVec*>; _call_evidence silently dropped the ambiguous candidates. F3: MSL deque<T> stores void** so all instantiations share one structural class; class 0aa8bf129b24d47ebd50 was named deque<LOBBY_STATE> although 9 of its 12 DIEs are deque<void const*> base subobjects. Template names must attach only to DIEs the evidence reaches, ambiguity must be a contradiction, and a member or base that contradicts its owner's template arguments must block.

resolution.summary: type_identity.py no longer infers template names from symbols: shared spellings (several qualified candidates or a template base) get names only on DIEs that method or call-site evidence reaches, across every compile-unit copy of the caller's class; ambiguous call-site receivers are contradictions; a member or base that contradicts its owner's template arguments is a blocking conflict. queue and stack are now provisional, and class 0aa8bf129b24d47ebd50 names only its 3 reached DIEs deque<CZOnlineLobby::LOBBY_STATE> while the 9 base subobjects stay provisional. Symbol candidates now include qualified names inside template arguments.

issues.summary: Import-plan identity names layout-identical template instantiations from partial evidence

issues.details: F4: _type_rows and _function_rows use Die.integer() for mod_user_def_type and mod_fund_type, which are blocks, so 11,944 member mod_user_def_type and 2,625 mod_fund_type references are null; user_def_type offsets and fund_type codes share one untagged type_reference field; array rows carry no decoded element type. The apply item needs typed references.

resolution.summary: Import plan schema 4 replaces type_reference fields with descriptors {modifiers, die_offset, fund_type} for members, type rows, parameters, locals, returns, and variables, and decodes array dimensions and element types. All 14,569 modified member types keep their modifiers; no member type is null.

issues.summary: Import-plan type references drop modifiers and mix DIE offsets with fundamental types

issues.details: F5 three-operand mult/multu write rd; F6 REGIMM bltzal/bgezal(l) write ra; F7 branch-likely delay slots are applied on the fall-through path where they are annulled; F8 unconditional b (beq zero,zero) does not end the block; F9 intra-function j and BC0/BC2 targets are not merge points; F10 a0 is assumed to be this for every qualified function, including those DWARF shows have no this. Measured impact on the current plan: none, but the tracer must be correct before more evidence depends on it.

resolution.summary: The R5900 tracer treats mult/multu as writing rd, REGIMM link branches as calls writing ra, annuls branch-likely delay slots on fall-through, ends blocks at unconditional b, treats intra-function j and BC0/BC1/BC2 targets as merge points, and skips callers and callees that DWARF shows without this. Unit tests cover each form.

issues.summary: R5900 call-site tracer misdecodes several instruction forms

issues.details: An awaiting_acceptance item can only be accepted. When independent review of socom:work:debug-type-foundation found defects, no registered command could return it for rework while recording the findings.

resolution.summary: Added progress work reject: an independent reviewer returns an awaiting_acceptance item to ready with a reason and evidence; the rejected handoff, its evidence, and any Ghidra receipt move to review_history; handoff owners cannot reject. Used by socom-verifier at tracker revision 10.

issues.summary: Tracker has no governed route to reject a handoff

issues.details: F11 resolution does not signal when the round cap is reached without convergence; F12 mwdemangle renders pointers to functions as R (*)(...)* and member-function pointers awkwardly, and these strings become Ghidra paths; F13 tests do not cover branch-likely, three-operand mult, b ending a block, or template contradictions; tests/tools/test_cli.py test_progress_next_accepts_trailing_json hard-codes the next work item and fails whenever tracker state moves on.

resolution.summary: Resolution raises when it does not converge within 16 rounds; function and member-function pointers render as declarators (void (C::*)(args)); tests cover branch-likely, three-operand mult, b ending a block, j merge points, template arguments, and review regressions; test_progress_next compares against the tracker's own next_work. The independence audit no longer mistakes this workspace's tests/tools/*.py paths for foreign tool entry points.

issues.summary: Identity resolution, rendering, and tests need fail-closed and coverage fixes

issues.details: Second review of socom:work:debug-type-foundation (accepted at tracker revision 14) found latent tracer risks with no effect on the accepted plan. (1) Metrowerks passes the hidden struct-return pointer in a0 and this in a1 (getloc__Q23std8ios_baseCFv: jal ...; lw a1,0x20(a1)); mangling does not mark static methods; only 753 of 5,963 qualified functions in main have DWARF, so 7,198 of 8,308 call records come from callers whose receiver register cannot be confirmed (type_identity.py:547-566). (2) For self-call path (0,) only the owner DIE is excluded, so a same-spelling base at offset 0 (MSL deque<T*> derives from deque<void const*>) could take the derived name (type_identity.py:604-609); 0 of 2,341 such records produce a candidate today. (3) is_template_name inspects only the last component, so symbol inference can still name types nested in class templates (type_identity.py:206; test_import_plan.py:80-85); the only instance, std::__red_black_tree<1>::anchor, is correct. (4) The template-argument self-check covers only by-value members whose spelling equals an argument base and skips cv-qualified arguments (type_identity.py:795-825).
issues.summary: Call-site tracer can misread a0 for struct returns, unmarked static methods, and same-spelling bases

issues.details: Second-review low findings: (5) no unit test exercises _template_argument_conflicts, ambiguity-to-contradiction, or the self-call exclusion, and the integration test does not assert stack is provisional; (6) reject_work compares the unstripped reviewer to the handoff owner but stores reviewer.strip(), so a space-padded owner name passes and is recorded as a self-rejection; reject also accepts empty evidence (tracker.py:956-963); (7) the independence-audit lookbehind exempts any path ending in tests/tools/*.py, not only this repository's (source.py:27).
issues.summary: Review follow-ups: identity test gaps, reject owner comparison, and test-path exemption breadth

issues.details: live_preflight in tools/_socom/ghidra.py compares get_current_program_info.executable_path (Ghidra's Program Information 'Executable Location', fixed at import) with the absolute path of this checkout's support/socom.elf. Moving the workspace or the soCOM project to another machine or checkout root fails preflight with 'program executable path does not identify support/socom.elf' although the program is unchanged: on the second workstation the semantic receipt equals the baseline 76e6ddc1...6e96c and the stored 'Executable SHA256' option equals the reference 00c9cee7...3d4f8a. The check binds identity to a machine-specific path, contrary to the portability rule in AGENTS.md, and blocks every live Ghidra item. Identity should come from the stored Executable SHA256, not the import path.

resolution.summary: live_preflight now reads the Program Information option group (get_program_options) and requires the stored 'Executable SHA256' to equal the reference SHA-256; the import path ('Executable Location' / executable_path) is no longer compared, and the report exposes program_executable_sha256. Tests cover a foreign import path with the reference hash (passes) and a missing or foreign hash (fails). docs/reconstruction/GHIDRA.md updated. On the second workstation: ghidra preflight --strict ok, doctor --infrastructure-only --ghidra ok, tools suite 96 passed with only the known GUIDANCE.md surface failure.

issues.summary: Ghidra live preflight requires the program's recorded import path to equal this checkout

issues.details: The GhidraMCP delete_data_type endpoint documents 'Fails if the type is referenced', but deleting /undefined1[12] (a baseline type applied to defined data) succeeded and cleared 269 data items: the semantic receipt data index fell from 51,523 to 51,254 while the type index still matched after the array type was recreated. The unsaved program was reverted by closing without saving and reopening; the receipt again equals 76e6ddc1...6e96c. Any tool or worker that deletes Ghidra types must restrict deletion to types it created in the same run, never pre-existing names, and must confirm cleanup with a full semantic receipt rather than the type list alone.
issues.summary: Bridge delete_data_type clears data applications instead of refusing referenced types

issues.details: _scoped_type_facts in tools/_socom/ghidra.py treated only identical-case names as ambiguous and recorded whatever get_struct_layout returned. The bridge ignores case and truncates names at '&', so the handoff receipt for socom:work:debug-type-foundation-apply recorded LINE_DATA's 20-byte layout for /project/line_data (4 bytes) and Action's 2-byte layout for /project/CAiMap/action (40 bytes), and two '&' names silently became size-only. Found by socom-verifier; the item was rejected at tracker revision 19.

resolution.summary: _scoped_type_facts now counts names ignoring case (ambiguous-name), records a layout or enum only when the bridge reports the requested name and size (else mismatched-readback), marks unresolvable names unreadable-name and unions/function definitions no-component-readback. tests/tools/test_ghidra.py covers each case including line_data/LINE_DATA; GHIDRA.md documents the case-insensitive lookup and '&' truncation.

issues.summary: Scoped receipt facts trusted case-insensitive and truncated bridge lookups

issues.details: The schema 4 plan records only the return type of subroutine_type rows. 19 of the 20 subroutine types reached from the type foundation have 1-3 formal_parameter children in the raw DWARF (e.g. DIE 0x1851 has a parameter at 0x1861), so socom:work:debug-type-foundation-apply created /project/anonymous/@subroutine@* function definitions with unspecified (...) parameters. issues.details: Enum element values are decoded signed at the enum width, which preserves the bit patterns but yields 48 negative values, e.g. 1-byte EQUIP_ITEM has EQUIP_NONE=-1 beside EQUIP_HEAVYWEAPON=-116 (0x8c, i.e. 140 if unsigned). Settle each enum's signedness from load/compare evidence (lb/lbu, slt/sltu) before relying on the displayed values.
issues.summary: Signedness of one-byte enum values is not settled by code evidence

issues.details: Fund type 0xA510 is proven 16 bytes wide and 16-byte aligned and is applied as uint16, but DWARF 1 carries no typedef for it; 'unsigned' rests on the member name _word128::u128 and the SDK spelling u_long128. Confirm signedness from code evidence or a typed provider header.
issues.summary: Signedness of the 128-bit fundamental type 0xA510 rests on a member name

Record packing in receipts or convert them to non-packed layouts once the bridge allows it.

issues.details: Only digests of the 210-type baseline index are stored, so an independent reviewer cannot confirm that pre-existing types were left unchanged except through the apply's own before/after check. issues.details: The accepted receipt 2b4eea98...2b9d for socom:work:debug-type-foundation-apply records no members for 45 of 840 scoped types: 17 names that are not unique ignoring case (line_data/LINE_DATA, CAiMap/action/Action, nested node, entry, iterator, sentry, generic_iterator<1>, two @union@0x4), 2 names the bridge truncates at '&' (Metrowerks alloc_ptr and compressed_pair_imp over list_deleter node&), and 26 unions/function definitions. issues.details: 210 local_variable DIEs inside functions carry DW_OP_ADDR locations (function statics). They stay in the function's locals with address storage but are not listed in receipt_scope.globals, so a batch apply would not bind them. Batch 001 has none.
issues.summary: Function-level static locals with fixed addresses never reach receipt globals

issues.details: In batch 001, 10 of 22 functions list fewer formal parameters than their mangled signatures: the 7 CGameState virtuals have no parameter DIEs (no this, Tick's float, OnPush/OnPop's int); both __dt omit the hidden short destructor flag in a1 (move s1,a1 then 16-bit sign extension); basic_string::__ct omits const allocator&. parameter_storage still reports recorded for empty or partial lists. Prototypes for the apply must come from the mangled signature and the Metrowerks calling convention, with DWARF names and types where they exist.

issues.details: 12 batch 001 variables (__RTTI__* and __vt__*; 7 present: __RTTI__5CGame, __RTTI__8COurGame, __RTTI__10CGameState, four __vt__ tables) reference member-less anonymous @anonN structure DIEs with no ghidra_path, so the plan offers no Ghidra type to apply. A typing policy for Metrowerks RTTI and vtable objects is needed before applying globals.
issues.summary: RTTI and vtable globals are typed by member-less anonymous structures

issues.details: Applying batch plans (functions and globals) needs: entry-relative stack offsets (frame size only in raw attribute 0x2010, e.g. 011d000000043000000007 = sp+0x30, while locals are post-prologue sp-relative); prototypes from mangled signatures plus calling convention including hidden parameters; a naming choice between DWARF spellings and demangled names for static members while preserving mangled aliases; and rules for replacing current live data (__RTTI__8COurGame/__RTTI__10CGameState are 4-byte pointers, gopt is undefined1, vtables undefined1[N], zero-fill globals have no data). Also: variable qualified_name keeps the raw DWARF spelling while the demangled form is only in symbol_qualified_names, and symbols lists zero-size linker markers such as __static_init_end.
issues.summary: Batch apply needs frame size, prototype policy, and live-data retyping rules

issues.details: map_zero_fill called the bridge's run_analysis, which runs AutoAnalysisManager.reAnalyzeAll over all initialized memory (not incremental analysis as claimed). The handoff at tracker revision 30 saved its effects: 25 four-byte string literals typed as pointers into .bss (e.g. @3845 'POS' at 0x449bf0), a false 42-entry Address Table at 0x2045e580, +221 data rows and +12 Address Table bookmarks outside main.bss. The item was rejected at revision 31; Ghidra's undo history was cleared by the save, so the program must be restored from a fresh baseline import.

resolution.summary: map_zero_fill runs no analyzer: it adds only relocation-proven references (16,333: R_MIPS_LO16 paired with the latest HI16 of the same symbol, R_MIPS_GPREL16 from the .reginfo gp, R_MIPS_32 words), typed by opcode, and fails if the function index, data outside the new block, or bookmarks change. New ghidra restore-accepted replays accepted applies on a fresh baseline import and requires their accepted receipts to reproduce. GHIDRA.md records that run_analysis and reanalyze re-analyze all initialized memory.

issues.summary: ghidra map-zero-fill ran a full reanalysis that invented pointers and was saved

issues.details: relocation_references paired each R_MIPS_LO16 with the most recent R_MIPS_HI16 of its symbol in .relmain order. Metrowerks interleaves HI16s of one section symbol across functions (e.g. .bss@0x58a248 upper halves 0x59 and 0x5b) and lists some after their LO16, so three saved references were false: 0x411dac and 0x411db4 -> 0x5aa268 and 0x412c7c -> 0x5aa25c instead of RelUdpTopOfPendingSendBuffer 0x58a268 and CommID 0x58a25c. Found by socom-verifier; rejected at tracker revision 34.

resolution.summary: tools/_socom/mips_flow.py pairs each LO16 with the lui whose write of its base register reaches the site (intra-function CFG with delay slots, annulled branch-likely slots, always-taken b, call clobbers after the delay slot, dead padding, jump-table targets, addu/move index arithmetic; unsized crt0 uses label spans). 24,221 of 24,231 LO16s resolve; the 10 unresolved relocate .data/.rodata symbols, and an unresolved LO16 of a zero-fill symbol fails the step. Against the old pairing only the three B3 sites change among the 10,542 zero-fill LO16s. map-zero-fill reconciles an existing block's references. Tests cover the three sites, crt0, delay-slot call clobbers, dead padding, and reconciliation.

issues.summary: Zero-fill references paired LO16 with the latest same-symbol HI16 in relocation order

issues.details: Non-blocking findings from the third zero-fill review (accepted at tracker revision 37); none changes any current target, and an independent conservative model agrees on all 24,231 LO16 targets. N1: no return edge after a likely call-branch's delay slot (the ELF has no REGIMM call-branches); syscall (165 sites) is not treated as clobbering; unknown opcodes write no register; _dead skips any predecessor-less code (e.g. landing pads), not only nops. N2: relocation_references fails an unresolved LO16 only when its relocation symbol lies in the zero fill, not when some candidate target could; the ten current unresolved sites were checked by hand (two SetAiMode jump-table merges, lui 0x45 -> 0x451dc0; eight _vf*printf_r stack spills, lui 0x46 -> 0x467080/0x467270). Revisit before mips_flow pairs references outside the zero fill.
issues.summary: mips_flow has latent modelling gaps and the zero-fill guard tests the LO16 symbol, not its target

issues.details: From the batch 001 acceptance (tracker revision 40). (N1) execute_batch_program checks function renames for clashes but not global renames, although GHIDRA.md promises collision-safe names; __RTTI__5CGame (2 copies) and __RTTI__10CGameState (6 copies) are file-local objects, so later batches would create duplicate CGame::__RTTI / CGameState::__RTTI labels unchecked. (N3) mangled secondary labels are trusted from create_label's status and not read back, and their recorded source changes from IMPORTED to USER_DEFINED. (N7) _Types.render turns every DWARF modifier into a pointer instead of rejecting const/volatile as type_apply does (safe for this ELF, which has only pointer/reference modifiers). Batch 001 itself is unaffected: the verifier confirmed all 29 names unique and all 29 mangled labels live.

issues.details: From the batch 001 acceptance (tracker revision 40). readable_function_name renders std::basic_string<...>::basic_string for the constructor at 0x1415f0 and also for overloads at 0x14d890 and 0x14d9c0; later batches will be refused the name (name already used) and keep only the mangled name. issues.details: From the batch 001 acceptance (tracker revision 40). restore-accepted replays only debug-import-apply-foundation items; it already has no route for socom:work:ghidra-zero-fill-memory, and accepted debug-import-apply-batch items add a second kind. issues.details: From the batch 001 acceptance (tracker revision 40). Prototypes and data types whose type names contain ',' (template arguments such as basic_string<char, std::char_traits<char>, std::allocator<char>>) are recorded skips because set_function_prototype/apply_data_type parse names textually. issues.details: Planning batch 10 (socom:debug-batch:873c518eab3c45871ed4) showed three defects before any apply. (1) Metrowerks emits global_variable DIEs of subroutine type at the entries of compiler-generated member functions (__ct/__dt of C2DOrderItem, CMD_TABLE, CSubMenu at 0x1747e0, 0x177990, 0x178cc0, 0x178d50, 0x17bbd0, 0x17c4d0); the plan marked them present globals and the batch program would have applied @subroutine data with clear_existing at those entries (clearing their instructions) and renamed the functions through rename_label. (2) Each global repeats once per declaring compile unit (theMission, _impure_ptr, goptarg, ...), giving duplicate program entries. (3) Function parameter and return types reference type DIEs in other compile units, which the plan omitted, so 13 of 21 prototypes skipped with 'DIE outside the plan'.

resolution.summary: import_plan marks subroutine-typed objects at FUNC entries status function-object (never present or in receipt globals) and adds referenced_only type rows for out-of-batch DIEs named by functions and present variables (with members, following unnamed array elements). build_batch_program folds per-unit rows by address (types must agree), refuses globals inside a function or of function type, and lists only status absent in absent_variables; execute_batch_program refuses addresses audit_global reports as code, leaves globals that already have the type and length (unchanged), and skips global renames whose readable name is used at another address (.symtab names, live function and defined-data names, this run's names). Batch 001's plan and program regenerate byte-identically (plan 5668ec79, program e43be2c1). Tests cover each case; DWARF_IMPORT.md and GHIDRA.md document them.

issues.summary: Batch plans typed function-entry objects as globals and lacked cross-unit types

issues.details: Batch 10 review (tracker revision 42): recoResult at 0x48a040 is typed by a 56-byte anonymous class rendered @class@d37844a018, which has no match in the live program (GET list_data_types), so the batch apply will record a skip instead of typing it. Find why the accepted foundation apply omitted this structural class (and whether other anonymous classes are missing) and add it through a governed type apply.
issues.summary: Type foundation did not create anonymous class @class@d37844a018 used by recoResult

issues.details: Batch 10 acceptance (tracker revision 46). (1) Metrowerks DWARF 1 parameter records omit const that the mangled signature keeps, e.g. getopt__FiPCPcPCc is applied as (int, char * *, char *) instead of (int, char * const *, const char *); the mangled secondary label preserves it, but prototypes should reconcile cv-qualifiers from the mangled name once the bridge can spell them. (2) Derived arrays of builtin elements created by apply_data_type (char *[4], char[30]) resolve into the root/builtin category rather than a stable project category; decide whether derived types need a governed category.
issues.summary: Applied prototypes drop const that mangled names carry; derived types land in the root category

issues.details: Planning batch 11 (socom:debug-batch:1c9907d6eef3a9fccef6) before any apply. (1) build_batch_program mapped DWARF parameter i to mangled position i, but Metrowerks DWARF omits parameters anywhere: LoadTextures__10OrdersMenuFPQ23zdb6CWorldP7C2DFont records only font, giving (C2DFont *, C2DFont *) instead of (CWorld *, C2DFont *); HandleRecoCmd__10OrdersMenuFiiiiPc records three of four ints and lastString, giving (int, int, int, char *, char *). (2) render_demangled read a class parameter's 'qualifier' while mwdemangle reports 'components', so every class-typed mangled-filled parameter skipped as class ''. (3) Classes named only by the mangled signature had no identity in the plan (_zrdr, _zanim_cmd_hdr, zdb::CWorld). Batches 001 and 10 had no partial DWARF lists (checked), so their applied prototypes are unaffected.

resolution.summary: build_batch_program places DWARF parameters as an ordered subsequence of the mangled signature allowed by pointer depth and class name or builtin width (_Types.shape/mangled_shape/_compatible); a DWARF parameter keeps its name and type only where every placement agrees, other positions take the mangled type, and no placement is a recorded skip. render_demangled reads components. import_plan adds a referenced_only row for each class a short-DWARF function's mangled signature names, when exactly one identity carries the name. Batch 001 and 10 plans and programs regenerate byte-identically; batch 11 yields 23 of 24 prototypes with LoadTextures (this, CWorld *, C2DFont *font) and HandleRecoCmd (this, int x4, char *lastString). Tests cover the shapes and both functions.

issues.summary: Batch programs assumed DWARF lists the leading parameters and dropped mangled class parameters

issues.details: Batch 11 plan review (tracker revision 49), non-blocking for batch 11. (1) batch_apply._compatible rejects 22 of 405 full-length mangled/DWARF lists binary-wide: 20 MSL wide-char functions because DWARF spells wchar_t as ushort and BUILTIN_SIZES has no wchar_t/schar width, and __list_deleter::erase/insert (0x17c580, 0x17c630) because DWARF records the by-value iterator as pointer_to with a provisional name; those prototypes would now skip instead of applying by index, and in a partial list a wchar_t could be uniquely placed on a wrong 2-byte position. (2) import_plan first_die takes the first DIE of a structural class rather than one whose identity carries the wanted name, and does nothing when the class is already carried, so for classes shared by several names (compressed_pair_imp has 3 identities) the scope could list another name's path; batch 11's picks (_zanim_cmd_hdr, _zrdr, zdb::CWorld) are correct. (3) Placement uses itertools.combinations; worst case today is 55 combinations. (4) HandleRecoCmd keeps param_2..param_5 although the assembly identifies subjectID/verbID/objectID at positions 3-5; ambiguous placements could use argument-register reads to name parameters. (5) bool resolves through Ghidra's built-in type manager (DataTypeParser.findDataType), adding a root /bool type outside the receipt scope.
issues.summary: Parameter alignment rejects wchar_t and by-value iterator placements; mangled-class DIE choice ignores the name

issues.details: Batch 11 apply acceptance (tracker revision 52). (1) Where DWARF supplies a boolean (fundamental 0x3) prototypes use uchar (C2D::SetCanHandleInput, SetUseFrameBufferAlpha, OrdersMenu::AllCollapse); where only the mangled signature does, they use Ghidra bool (C2D::TickZAnimCmd bool *). Both are one byte; settle one spelling consistent with the Metrowerks ABI. (2) Derived pointer/array types created by applies (batch 001: 3, batch 10: 12, batch 11: /bool, /bool *, /project/C2DAnimCmdHdr *) are bound only by the unscoped type-index digest, not listed in receipt scopes as AGENTS.md function-workflow step 9 asks for changed types.
issues.summary: bool is spelled uchar from DWARF but bool from mangled names; derived types stay outside receipt scopes

issues.details: Batch 12 plan review (tracker revision 55). (1) OrdersMenu::SetupTuple (0x17ac50) and EnableTuples (0x17aed0) are skipped for lack of receiver evidence (no DWARF this, not in a vtable), but the assembly proves a receiver: neither reads a0 yet each takes col from a1 (move s5,a1), and the only caller SetupTuples passes this (fp) in a0 and col in a1, with 8 stack doublewords for SetupTuple's 16 arguments. Receiver evidence could include caller argument setup and the first argument register a method actually reads. (2) DWARF fundamental type 0x2 (signed char) appears on 78 local 'init' variables and has no FUND_TYPES entry; inert while batch programs do not apply locals.
issues.summary: Receiver evidence ignores callers and argument-register use; DWARF fundamental 0x2 has no mapping

issues.details: Found by the batch 12 apply verifier (tracker revision 58). COurGame::StopPlay (0x140500) and StartPlay (0x140510) are `j 0x20e790 / j 0x20e7a0; nop`, which Ghidra models as thunks sharing their targets' signatures. Batch 001 set `void COurGame::StopPlay(COurGame * this)` on the thunks, so StopPlay__5CGameFv (0x20e790) and StartPlay__5CGameFv (0x20e7a0) now read `void __stdcall NAME(COurGame * this)`. Both targets have no DWARF record, so no batch will correct them. Receipts bind function names (index) and scoped details only, and the owner's snapshots captured signatures only for batch functions, so neither caught it. Batches 10-12 applied no prototype through a thunk (C2D::GetZAnimCmdType's tail call sets a0 in its delay slot and is not a thunk).

resolution.summary: Governed repair socom:work:ghidra-repair-batch-001-thunk-signatures (tracker schema 4->5 at revision 59, accepted by socom-verifier at revision 63, receipt 721a4437) restored StopPlay__5CGameFv and StartPlay__5CGameFv to undefined __stdcall NAME(void) (the bridge cannot set the import-time unknown convention; user decision). build_batch_program now records a thunk's prototype as a skip (_thunk_target: body j/b target; nop); the verifier's ELF-wide survey found the guard catches exactly the four DWARF-backed thunks, including BitmapReticule::Off/On (0x3ce4c0/0x3ce4d0) a later batch would have reached. Evidence for the proper CGame signatures is in issue 66b96708.

issues.summary: Batch 001 prototypes on two thunks rewrote CGame::StopPlay/StartPlay signatures

issues.details: The thunk repair (socom:work:ghidra-repair-batch-001-thunk-signatures) restored StopPlay__5CGameFv (0x20e790) and StartPlay__5CGameFv (0x20e7a0) to undefined __stdcall NAME(void) by user decision. Evidence for the proper signatures, for the ghidra-reconstruction stage: both sit in __vt__5CGame (slots 4 and 3); COurGame::StopPlay/StartPlay (DWARF void) are COurGame's thunks to them, and an override keeps its base's return type; StopPlay's body is `jr ra; sb zero,4(a0)` (no v0 write, a0 is this); StartPlay stores 1 to this+4, loads this->+8 into a1 and tail-jumps to 0x20be00 with a2=0. Supported: void __stdcall NAME(CGame * this) for both.
issues.summary: CGame::StopPlay/StartPlay can take evidence-backed void (CGame * this) signatures

issues.details: Repair acceptance (tracker revision 63). Ghidra flags 40 thunks (list_functions_enhanced isThunk). _thunk_target catches the 8-byte `j/b target; nop` shape only; 10 more live thunks sit inside symbols of 48-112 bytes (e.g. 0x193cd0 find<...CAiPath...> `b +8; nop`, 0x2241e0), where a branch target became a separate FUN_ function inside the symbol's extent: function-boundary defects for the reconstruction stage. None has DWARF, so no batch is affected today. A sturdier guard would refuse prototypes on any function that is a thunk in the live program. Also: the repair likely leaves a user-defined signature source where the import state was default/analysis (not measurable through the bridge).
issues.summary: Thunk guard recognises only 8-byte j/b thunks; Ghidra has 10 boundary-split thunks
